title: Calibration and measurement of mitochondrial pH in intact adult rat cardiomyocytes
protocol: Put an autoclaved 25 mm circular coverslip into a 35 mm dish using fine-tip forceps.
Add 100 μL laminin to the center of the coverslip for coating.
Spread the laminin over the coverslip using the pipette tip.
Gently place the plate into a 37°C incubator for 1–2 hours.
Count cardiomyocytes using a traditional Hemocytometer.
Dilute cells to a concentration of 2.5 × 10^5 / mL in M199 culture medium.
Add 200 μL of counted myocytes on a coated coverslip for cultivation.
Discard laminin with a pipette without allowing the coverslip to dry.
Add 200 μL cardiomyocyte suspension to the center of the coverslip.
Place the plate into a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator and wait for 2–4 h.
Gently discard the 200 μL medium after cells have attached.
Add 2 mL fresh M199 culture medium to the well.
Incubate the dish at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Remove the dish from the incubator after 2.5–3 hours.
Add 2 μL of 5 mM SNARF-1 AM into a well and mix gently three times by moving the dish backward and forward.
Incubate cells in media containing 5 μM SNARF-1 AM at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate SNARF-1 AM at room temperature for 45 min.
Discard the medium containing SNARF-1 AM.
Equilibrate myocytes with 2 mL KHB solution at room temperature (23°C–26°C) for 1.5 h.
Add 1 μl of 200 mM MitoTracker Green molecular probe to the dish and mix well by gently moving the dish backward and forward three times.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 30 min for co-staining mitochondria.
Pick the coverslip up using fine-tip forceps.
Place the coverslip on a Kimwipes cleaning paper to dry the bottom of the coverslip.
Insert the coverslip into the magnetic bottom of the chamber and secure with the magnetic top.
Add 1 ml pH7.0 calibration solution into the chamber using a pipette.
Equilibrate for 5 minutes.
Add one drop of oil on the 63× objective lens.
Place the imaging chamber onto the microscope stage above the objective lens.
Find and focus the cell sample in the eyepieces.
Move the cell sample to the center field of vision.
Set the imaging parameters of Zen software.
Excite SNARF-1 AM at 543 nm using Lambda scan mode of Zeiss LSM 880.
Collect emission spectra of SNARF-1 AM from 545 to 750 nm.
Acquire images at a resolution of 1024 × 1024.
Set gain between 450 and 600, pinhole between 50 and 200, and laser intensity between 5% and 8%.
Discard calibration solution in chamber on the stage.
Wash the chamber once for 2 minutes with 1 mL pH 7.4 calibration solution.
Add 1 mL pH 7.4 calibration solution to equilibrate for 5 minutes.
Repeat steps 18–20 three times to collect emission spectra of SNARF-1 AM in pH 8.0, 8.5, and 9.0.
Measure mitochondrial pH by confocal imaging.
Set imaging parameters of Zen software for dual excitation images of MitoTracker Green probe and SNARF-1 AM.
Excite MitoTracker Green at 488 nm and collect fluorescence from 505 to 545 nm.
Excite SNARF-1 AM at 543 nm and collect emission spectra >615 nm (S2).
Acquire images at a resolution of 1024 × 1024.
Set gain between 450 and 600, pinhole between 50 and 200, and laser intensity between 5% and 8%.
Set cells in the chamber for imaging by adding pH 7.4 KHB solution.
Find and focus on the cell sample using the eyepieces.
Choose only the 488 nm channel to pre-setup relevant imaging parameters by live scan.
Acquire bright field image of myocytes.
Load myocytes with MitoTracker green.
Obtain merged image of myocytes and mitochondria.
Select rod cardiomyocytes with clear mitochondrial pattern for imaging.
Start acquiring 2D images at intervals of 30 seconds.
After the fourth frame, add 10 mM NH4Cl to the calibration solution.
Wait for automatic image capture after adding NH4Cl.
After the fourteenth frame, add 300 nM FCCP to the calibration solution.
Wait for automatic image capture after adding FCCP.
Stop acquisition after the twenty-third frame and save images.
Open ZEN software and choose ‘ZEN image processing’ option.
Open cell image in ZEN software.
Choose the ‘Profile’ button in ZEN software (green arrow indicated).
Zoom into the image in ZEN software.
Select a specific mitochondrion using the definition tool in ZEN software (red arrow indicated).
Display intensity of selected mitochondria in left panel of ZEN software.
Export data from ZEN software.
Calculate mean of S1 and S2 intensities.
Divide S1 by S2 to calculate mitochondrial pH according to calibration line.
